Fully shorten the straps and stand facing the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other and wrists straight. Pull the shoulders down and back, bend the elbows and bring the hands beside the lower chest. Walk the feet toward the anchor until the back is engaged, then extend the arms so the body leans away in one straight line from ears through ankles. Keep the straps taut.

Maintain the active plank as the arms straighten and the body lowers away from the anchor. Initiate the return by drawing the shoulder blades down and back, then drive the elbows straight back beside the ribs until the hands finish beside the lower chest. Extend the arms slowly to repeat.

Keep the head aligned with the spine, shoulders away from the ears and hips level. The standard Low Row uses a neutral grip and low elbow path. Walk the feet toward the anchor for more resistance or away for less; do not change difficulty by bending at the hips.

Fully shorten the straps and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing the floor, wrists straight and arms extended in front of the shoulders. Set the shoulders down and back and lean away in a straight active plank with the straps taut.

Initiate by drawing the shoulder blades down and back. Pull with the elbows travelling about 45 degrees away from the torso until the hands reach the sides of the middle chest. Pause, then extend the arms slowly without losing the plank.
The Mid Row sits between the Low Row and High Row: palms down and elbows about 45 degrees from the ribs. Walk the feet toward the anchor for more load or away for less; do not bend at the hips.

Fully shorten the straps and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing the floor, wrists straight and arms extended. Set the shoulders down and back and lean away in a straight active plank with the straps taut.

Draw the shoulder blades down and back, then pull with the elbows rising to shoulder height. Bend the elbows about 90 degrees and drive the knuckles back until the hands finish beside the shoulders. Extend the arms slowly to return.
Use the shoulder-height elbow path to distinguish the High Row from the Mid and Low Rows. Keep the palms down and finish without adding the extra external rotation used in a Face Pull or W Fly.

Set the straps to fully shortened in single-handle mode and stand facing the anchor with a wide, stable stance. Hold the handle with a neutral grip (palm facing inward), keep the wrist straight, extend the working arm and square the shoulders and hips to the anchor in an active plank.

Lower the body by extending the working arm while resisting rotation. Drive the elbow low beside the ribs to pull the chest toward the handle, then return slowly with shoulders and hips square. Move the feet toward the anchor to increase the load.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.

Set the straps to fully shortened and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), wrists straight and arms extended. Set the shoulders down and back, keep the straps taut and hold an active plank.

Extend both arms to lower the body, then pull one handle toward the ribs while the other arm remains long; alternate sides without twisting the hips. Return each arm slowly and maintain the active plank. Adjust the foot position to change the body angle and load.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.

Fully shorten the straps and stand facing the anchor with the feet wider than hip width. Hold both handles with a neutral grip, extend the arms and lean back in a straight plank. Keep the straps taut and begin with the shoulders square to the anchor.

Extend the arms and rotate the ribs and pelvis away from the anchor while pivoting on the balls of the feet. Reverse the rotation, square the hips and chest to the anchor and pull both elbows beside the ribs until the handles reach the lower chest. Extend the arms and rotate away again under control.

Turn the body as one unit instead of twisting through the lower back. Keep the wrists straight and shoulders away from the ears. Use a more upright body angle if the hips sag or the straps lose tension.

Set the straps to mid length in single-handle mode and stand facing the anchor with a wide stance. Hold the handle with a neutral grip (palm facing inward) and a straight wrist, extend the working arm and reach the free arm toward the anchor while keeping the strap taut.

Reach the free hand toward the floor and rotate away as the working arm lengthens. Drive the working elbow back, rotate the chest toward the anchor and reach the free arm up the strap. Reverse under control, using the trunk and back together.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with palms up, wrists straight and arms extended at shoulder height. Lean back in a straight plank and lift the elbows slightly above shoulder height so the upper arms remain fixed.

Without moving the upper arms, bend both elbows and bring the pinky sides of the hands toward the temples. Pause without bending the wrists, then slowly extend the elbows until the arms are straight and the straps remain taut.
Keep the elbows high, shoulders down and ribs stacked over the pelvis. Walk the feet toward the anchor for more resistance or away for less; do not let the hips fold.

Set the straps to mid length in single-handle mode and stand facing the anchor in a stable stance. Hold the handle palm up/toward the face with a straight wrist, lift the working elbow to shoulder height and extend the arm while keeping the shoulders and hips square.

Keep the working upper arm lifted and still as the elbow bends and the pinky travels toward the temple. Extend slowly without dropping the elbow, bending the wrist or allowing the torso to rotate; repeat on the opposite side.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles palms up/toward the face with straight wrists and elbows lifted at shoulder height. Extend both arms into an active plank while keeping equal pressure on the straps.

Keep both upper arms lifted as one elbow bends and that hand travels toward the temple. Extend it under control, then alternate arms without dropping either elbow, twisting the wrists or allowing the torso to rotate.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), wrists straight and arms extended. Keep the shoulders down and the elbows ready to travel beside the ribs before the curl toward the chest.
Draw the elbows back beside the ribs, then curl the handles toward the chest in the clutch position. Reverse the sequence under control while keeping the body aligned and the straps taut.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a pronated grip (palms down/away), wrists straight and elbows lifted near shoulder height. Extend the arms while maintaining an active plank and continuous strap tension.
Maintain a palms-down grip and keep the upper arms fixed while curling the handles toward the forehead. Extend the elbows slowly and keep the wrists straight and shoulders down.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.
TRX High Row to External Rotation
TRX Face Pull with External Rotation

Set the straps to fully lengthened and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a pronated grip (palms down) and straight wrists, arms extended at shoulder height. Use an offset stance, set the shoulders down and back and keep the straps taut.
Pull the handles toward the face with the elbows high, then externally rotate so the hands finish beside the ears. Reverse the movement slowly, keeping the shoulders down and the ribs stacked.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an offset stance. Begin with the arms extended, palms down and wrists straight. Keep the shoulders down and back and maintain an active plank with continuous strap tension.

Keeping the elbows straight and wrists neutral, allow the arms to travel forward as the body lowers in one line. Drive the hands up and apart to roughly 45 degrees overhead so the arms form a Y, with the thumbs leading slightly upward; return slowly without shrugging or arching.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an offset stance. Begin at the finish position with straight arms extended to the sides in a T, palms forward and wrists straight. Pull the shoulders down and back and keep the straps taut.

Keeping the elbows straight and wrists neutral, allow the arms to travel forward as the body lowers in one line. Pull through the shoulders and drive the knuckles back until the arms reopen into a T with the palms forward. Return slowly without bending the elbows or thrusting the hips.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an offset stance. Begin with the elbows bent about 90 degrees, hands above the shoulders, palms facing the anchor and wrists straight so the arms form a W. Keep the shoulders down and the straps taut.

Keeping the elbows bent about 90 degrees, rotate the forearms and hands downward from the shoulders as the body lowers. Drive the knuckles back above the shoulders to reform the W, keeping the palms toward the anchor and the shoulders away from the ears.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an offset stance. Hold the handles with straight wrists and arms extended overhead in an I, with the palms facing inward toward each other. Keep the ribs stacked, shoulders down and straps taut.

Keeping the elbows straight and wrists neutral, lower the body as the arms travel forward. Drive the hands overhead until the arms align beside the ears in an I, palms facing inward; return slowly without arching the lower back.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.
TRX Y Fly to T Fly

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an offset stance. Hold one handle in each hand with straight arms, wrists neutral and palms facing forward. Begin tall with the arms overhead in a Y, shoulders pulled down and back, ribs stacked and continuous tension in the straps.

Keeping the elbows straight, lower the body by allowing the arms to travel forward and down. Drive the knuckles back and open the arms to a T at shoulder height. Lower again with straight arms, then drive the knuckles overhead to return to the Y. Alternate the T and Y returns without bending the elbows.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and do not arch the lower back. Use the offset stance to assist only as needed. Step farther from the anchor or reduce the lean to make the movement easier.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an offset stance. Hold the handles with straight wrists and begin with the arms in the programmed Y position. Maintain tension while transitioning to palms-forward in the T and palms-toward-anchor with elbows bent in the W.

Complete a controlled Y fly, return to straight arms, then open into a T with palms forward. Return again and finish with the elbows bent about 90 degrees and hands above the shoulders to form a W. Reset to straight arms between positions.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to fully shortened and position the body directly under the anchor. Hold the handles with an overhand grip (palms facing away), wrists straight and arms extended overhead. Use a stable seated, kneeling or low-standing base and keep the straps evenly loaded.

Pull the shoulders down and drive the elbows toward the ribs to lift the chest between the handles. Use the legs only as much as needed, then lower until the arms are long while maintaining shoulder control.
Keep continuous strap tension and move at a pace that preserves balance and alignment. Start with a smaller range and stop the set when the position can no longer be maintained.

Set the straps to fully shortened and position the body directly under the anchor. Hold the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing the body), wrists straight and arms extended overhead. Use a stable seated, kneeling or low-standing base and keep the straps evenly loaded.
With palms facing the body, bend the elbows and pull the chest toward the handles. Use the legs only as much as needed, then lower slowly to straight arms without shrugging.
Keep continuous strap tension and move at a pace that preserves balance and alignment. Start with a smaller range and stop the set when the position can no longer be maintained.

Set the straps to fully shortened and position the body under the anchor with the heels grounded and hips lifted. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), wrists straight and arms extended; maintain a rigid plank from shoulders to heels.

Keep the body rigid as the arms extend, then drive the elbows beside the ribs to pull the chest toward the handles. Lower slowly without allowing the hips to sag; change the body angle to scale the load.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.

Set the straps to long length and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand with the arms extended in front of the shoulders, palms down or facing each other and wrists straight. Choose a stable staggered or even stance, lean forward into the handles and form a straight active plank from ears through ankles. Keep the straps taut and positioned off the arms.

Maintain the plank while bending the elbows to lower the chest between the handles. Stop at about 90 degrees of elbow bend or before the shoulders roll forward. Drive through the palms and squeeze the chest to straighten the arms and return to the starting plank.
Keep the ribs stacked, glutes engaged and shoulders down and back. Prevent the straps from rubbing the upper arms. Step the feet backward toward the anchor for more resistance or forward for less.

Set the straps to fully lengthened in single-handle mode and stand facing away from the anchor in a wide or offset stance. Hold the handle palm down with a straight wrist, extend the working arm in front of the shoulder and square the hips and shoulders.

Bend the working elbow to lower the chest beside the handle while resisting torso rotation, then press back to straight arm. Keep the strap off the arm and the hips square; alter the foot position to scale the load.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to fully lengthened and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and arms extended in front of the shoulders. Use an offset stance and maintain even strap tension before alternating sides.
Lower into the press and extend one arm at a time while the other stabilizes, alternating without rotating the torso. Finish with both arms extended and maintain the plank throughout.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to fully lengthened and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold the handles with palms facing each other, wrists straight and arms extended in front of the chest with a slight fixed elbow bend. Use an offset stance and establish an active plank.
Open the arms in a wide arc with a slight, fixed elbow bend until the chest is level with the hands. Squeeze the chest to bring the handles back together, keeping the active plank and shoulders down.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to fully lengthened in single-handle mode and stand facing away from the anchor in a wide or offset stance. Hold the handle with the palm facing inward and a straight wrist, extend the arm in front of the chest with a slight elbow bend and square the hips and shoulders.
Open the arms in a wide arc with a slight, fixed elbow bend until the chest is level with the hands. Squeeze the chest to bring the handles back together, keeping the active plank and shoulders down.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to mid-calf and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand with palms down, arms extended in front of the shoulders and wrists straight. Choose a stable stance and lean forward into an active plank with the straps taut.

Keep the upper arms lifted and the elbows pointing forward as the elbows bend and the body lowers. Bring the thumbs toward the temples without allowing the elbows to spread. Drive through the palms and extend the elbows to return to the starting plank.
Only the elbows should move. Keep the hips aligned with the shoulders, ribs controlled and straps off the arms. Step forward to reduce resistance or backward toward the anchor to increase it.

Set the straps to mid-calf and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and extend the arms in front of the shoulders. Lean forward in a straight plank with the elbows pointing forward and the straps clear of the upper arms.

Keep the upper arms stationary while bending the elbows and bringing the thumbs toward the temples. Stop before the shoulders move or the back arches, then press through the handles and fully straighten the elbows.
Only the elbows move. Keep the head, ribs, hips and ankles aligned. Step forward to reduce resistance or backward toward the anchor to increase it.

Set the straps to mid-calf and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and extend the arms in front of the shoulders. Lean forward in a straight plank and keep the straps taut and off the arms.

Bend the elbows and sweep the hands past the sides of the head while the upper arms remain lifted. Continue the circular swimmer path until the hands reach behind the head, then reverse the same path and extend the elbows to the start.
Use a small, pain-free circle and keep the shoulders down. Do not arch the lower back or allow the elbows to flare wider than you can control.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing away from the anchor in a strong forward-leaning plank. Hold the handles beside the shoulders with palms facing forward/away from the body, wrists straight and elbows bent below the hands.
Bend the elbows and lower the head between the hands, keeping the hips, ribs and shoulders aligned. Press through the handles to extend the arms, then return with control.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor to place the toes in the foot cradles. Turn to the ground, place the hands under the shoulders and establish an active plank with the feet directly below the anchor.
Maintain the plank as the elbows bend and the chest lowers toward the floor. Press through the palms to return to straight arms, keeping the hips level and shoulders away from the ears.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor to place the toes in the foot cradles. Turn to the ground, place the hands under the shoulders and establish an active plank with the feet directly below the anchor.
Lower into a push-up and press back to plank. Draw both knees toward the chest for a suspended crunch, then extend the legs to a full plank before the next repetition; keep the hips controlled.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor to place the toes in the foot cradles. Turn to the ground, place the hands under the shoulders and establish an active plank with the feet directly below the anchor.
Pike the hips upward, then bend the elbows to lower the head between the hands. Press to straight arms and extend the hips back to the plank without losing shoulder position.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor to place the toes in the foot cradles. Turn to the ground, place the hands under the shoulders and establish an active plank with the feet directly below the anchor.
Maintain the plank as the elbows bend and the chest lowers toward the floor. Press through the palms to return to straight arms, keeping the hips level and shoulders away from the ears.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.

Fully lengthen the straps and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand with the arms extended in front of the shoulders and wrists straight. Choose a stable foot position, lean forward into an active plank and keep the straps taut and clear of the arms.

Lower into a chest press by bending both elbows while keeping the shoulders down and back. At the bottom, extend one arm laterally to the side while the other remains in the press position. Return to the start by pressing with the bent arm while sweeping the extended arm forward as a fly. Alternate sides on successive repetitions.
Keep the shoulders and hips square to the floor and do not rotate toward the reaching arm. Use a smaller body angle and shorter lateral reach until the trunk remains stable.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet about hip width. Hold the handles with a neutral grip, elbows below the shoulders and straps taut. Stand tall and use the handles only for balance or assistance.

Sit the hips back and down while bending the knees and keeping the heels grounded. Descend as far as the knees track with the toes and the spine stays long. Press through the whole feet to stand, assisting lightly with the arms only if needed.
Do not pull yourself up before the legs begin to drive. Reduce depth if the heels rise, knees collapse inward or the lower back rounds.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, elbows bent and stacked directly under the shoulders. Place the feet about hip-width apart with all four corners of each foot grounded. Stand tall with the straps taut and use only light support from the handles.

Sit the hips back and down while bending the knees and keeping the feet firmly planted. Descend only as far as the heels remain down and the knees track in the same direction as the toes. Drive through the whole feet, extend the knees and hips and return to a tall standing position.
Keep the chest lifted and avoid pulling the body upward with the arms. Reduce the depth if the heels rise, the knees collapse inward or the spine rounds.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand and extend the arms overhead with the elbows straight, arms in line with the ears and straps taut. Place the feet about hip-width apart and stand tall with the ribs stacked over the pelvis.

Keeping tension in the straps and the arms overhead, lower the hips back and down into a squat. Keep the feet firmly grounded and the knees tracking with the toes. Drive through the heels and midfeet to extend the hips and knees and return to standing.
Do not let the arms fall forward or the lower back arch. Reduce squat depth if the heels lift, the knees collapse inward or the arms cannot remain beside the ears.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Take a stance wider than shoulder width and turn the toes outward comfortably. Hold the handles with elbows below the shoulders and keep light tension in the straps.

Lower the hips between the heels while the knees bend and track in the same direction as the toes. Keep the chest lifted, then press through the heels and midfeet and squeeze the glutes to stand tall.
Keep both heels grounded and avoid forcing the toes excessively outward. Use the straps for balance, not to pull the torso upright.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet about hip width. Hold the handles lightly, keep the straps taut and lower into a controlled squat with the heels grounded.

From the lower half of the squat, rise 5 to 10 centimetres, then lower the same distance while maintaining knee and foot alignment. Complete the prescribed pulses, then press through the whole feet to stand fully.
Keep the pulse small and controlled. Do not bounce at the bottom, pull with the arms or allow the knees to collapse inward.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet about hip width. Hold the handles lightly, bend the elbows and keep the straps taut.

Sit the hips back and down into a squat, then drive through both feet and jump vertically. Land softly through the midfeet, bend the hips and knees to absorb the landing and re-establish the squat before the next repetition.
Use the straps for balance rather than pulling upward. Keep the knees tracking with the toes and replace the jump with a fast calf raise if the landing cannot remain quiet and controlled.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip and stack the elbows under the shoulders. Center the working foot with the anchor and distribute pressure across the heel, base of the big toe and base of the little toe. Extend the free leg forward with its heel off the floor. Keep the straps taut.

Sit the hips down and back over the working leg, allowing the knee to track over the middle of the foot. Lower only as far as balance and alignment can be maintained. Drive through the whole working foot and extend the hip and knee to return to standing.

Use the arms only for the assistance needed to maintain balance. Keep the working knee aligned with the toes and the chest lifted. Reduce depth before allowing the heel to rise or the knee to collapse inward.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles lightly, centre one foot with the anchor and extend the free leg forward with its heel off the floor.

Sit the hips back and down over the standing leg while the free leg remains forward. Lower only as far as the standing heel stays grounded and the knee tracks with the toes, then drive through the whole foot to stand.
Use the arms only for the assistance needed to balance. Reduce depth before the heel lifts, the knee collapses inward or the spine rounds.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip, elbows stacked below the shoulders and straps taut. Take a wide stance with both hips fully extended and the torso tall.

Shift the hips to one side and bend that hip and knee while keeping the opposite leg straight. Keep the working foot grounded and pull the toes of the straight leg upward toward the shin. Drive through the heel of the bent leg, fully extend the hips at center and repeat to the opposite side.
Keep the torso tall and the knee of the bent leg tracking with its toes. Use the straps for balance instead of pulling with the arms. Work only through a pain-free range.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet about hip width. Hold the handles with a neutral grip, straighten the arms and keep the straps taut.

Keep the arms connected to the torso rather than pulling with the shoulders. Pivot through the feet so the knees do not twist.

Set the straps to mid length and stand sideways to the anchor in an offset stance with the foot nearest the anchor forward. Hold one handle with the outside hand, cover that hand with the inside hand and draw both hands to the center of the chest. Keep the torso tall and the straps taut.

Rotate the hips and torso toward the anchor. From that rotated position, slowly extend the arms and allow the body to lean away while maintaining a stiff trunk and long spine. Rotate the body back to upright with the arms extended, then draw the hands back to the chest to reset.
Rotate around a tall vertical axis and pivot the feet as needed so the knees do not twist. Keep the shoulders down and control the return against the strap tension.

Set the straps to mid length and stand sideways to the anchor in a narrow stance. Place both hands inside the foot cradles with the palms pressed together and the thumbs wrapped over the top. Extend the arms at chest height with a slight bend in the elbows. Stack the head, shoulders and hips vertically and keep the body weight centered over the feet.

Brace the trunk and attempt to rotate toward the anchor, driving rotational force into the foot cradles without allowing the body or hands to move. Maintain this isometric anti-rotation contraction for 4 to 10 seconds, then gradually release the force before changing sides.

This is a stationary isometric exercise, not a repeated torso rotation. Keep constant strap tension, shoulders down and back and the eyes forward. Do not lean away from the anchor to create resistance.
Set the straps to mid length and stand sideways to the anchor in a golf-width stance. Hold both handles together with arms extended in front of the chest and straps taut.

Rotate the hips and chest away from the anchor as the hands sweep across the body to approximately shoulder height. Pivot both feet, then reverse the rotation under control and return the hands in front of the chest.
Lead with the hips and ribcage, not the arms. Keep the spine long and avoid forcing range through the lower back.

Set the straps to mid length and stand sideways to the anchor with a wide stance. Hold the handles together in the hand nearest the anchor and extend that arm upward; extend the free arm toward the floor.
Hinge at the hips and rotate the chest open while the free hand reaches toward the opposite foot and the strapped arm stays long overhead. Drive the hips forward and unwind to stand.
Keep both feet grounded and the spine long. Use a smaller reach if the knees turn inward or the lower back rounds.
Set the straps to mid length and stand sideways to the anchor with both hands holding the handles overhead. Place the inside foot in front of the outside foot and keep the arms close to the ears.
Allow the hips to arc away from the anchor while the torso forms a long side bend. Use the obliques to pull the hips back beneath the shoulders and return to a tall stance.
Keep the chest facing forward and shoulders away from the ears. Reduce the arc if the lower back pinches or the feet lose contact with the floor.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing away from the anchor. Hold one handle in each hand, extend the arms slightly behind the torso at or below shoulder height and use a staggered stance.
Step or lean forward until a gentle stretch is felt across the chest and front of the shoulders. Keep the elbows softly bent, breathe for the desired hold, then step back to release the tension.
Keep the ribs down and shoulders away from the ears. Lower the arms or reduce the forward step if the front of the shoulder feels pinched.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold both handles, straighten the arms and hinge the hips backward until the torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Press the hips away from the anchor and allow the chest to sink between the straight arms until a stretch is felt along the sides of the back. Breathe, then drive the hips forward and stand.
Keep the spine long, knees softly bent and shoulders away from the ears. Do not force the chest downward by arching the lower back.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles, bend the knees slightly and extend the arms at chest height.
Sit the hips backward and round the upper back while reaching the shoulder blades away from each other. Hold the stretch with light strap tension, then lift the chest and return to standing.
Keep the hips back and chin gently tucked. The movement should spread the shoulder blades without creating pain in the neck or lower back.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold both handles, soften the knees and keep the straps taut.
Sit the hips backward, allow the pelvis to tuck and gently round the lower back while the arms remain long. Breathe into the back of the waist, then untuck the pelvis and stand slowly.
Use only a gentle, pain-free range. Do not hang from the shoulders or force the spine into a deep rounded position.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold both handles overhead, place one foot slightly behind the other and keep the arms long.
Shift the hips to one side while the hands and ribcage arc to the opposite side until a stretch is felt along the side of the torso. Return to centre and repeat on the other side.
Keep both feet grounded and avoid rotating the chest. Lengthen through both sides of the waist before bending sideways.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet wider than hip width. Hold both handles at chest height with the arms long.
Rotate the chest and hips to one side while pivoting through the feet and allowing the opposite arm to lengthen. Pause in a comfortable range, then rotate through centre to the other side.
Move the pelvis and ribcage together and pivot instead of twisting through planted knees. Keep the shoulders down and straps taut.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Place one heel forward with the toes lifted, keep the other knee softly bent and hold the handles for balance.
Push the hips backward and hinge over the straight front leg until a stretch is felt behind the thigh. Keep the spine long, breathe, then drive the hips forward to stand before changing legs.
Square the hips to the anchor and stop before the spine rounds. The stretch should be in the hamstring, not behind the knee or in the lower back.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet just wider than hip width and toes turned out comfortably. Hold the handles with the arms long and straps taut.

Sit the hips between the heels into a deep squat while keeping the whole feet grounded. Use the straps to balance, gently shift weight side to side if comfortable, then press through the feet to stand.
Keep the knees tracking with the toes and the chest lifted. Reduce depth if the heels rise, the knees collapse or the hips or knees pinch.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Step into a split stance and hold the handles lightly with the torso tall.
Tuck the pelvis, squeeze the glute of the rear leg and shift the body forward until a stretch is felt across the front of the rear hip. Hold while breathing, then return and switch sides.
Keep the ribs stacked and rear heel lifted. Do not create the stretch by arching the lower back.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold both handles in one hand for balance, bend the opposite knee and grasp that ankle or foot with the free hand.
Draw the heel toward the glute while keeping the knees close and the pelvis gently tucked. Hold, then release the foot slowly and change sides.
Stand tall and keep the working thigh pointing down. Use a strap or smaller knee bend if the knee or lower back feels strained.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles, shift onto one leg and place the opposite ankle across the standing thigh above the knee.

Sit the hips backward as if into a single-leg squat while gently pressing the crossed knee outward. Hold when a stretch is felt in the outer hip, then drive through the standing foot to rise and switch sides.
Keep the standing heel down, spine long and crossed foot flexed. Reduce depth if the standing knee turns inward or the crossed knee feels pinched.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in a wide stance. Hold the handles with the arms long and straps taut.

Shift the hips toward one side and bend that knee while the opposite leg remains straight and both feet stay planted. Hold the inner-thigh stretch, then press through the bent leg to return to centre and switch sides.
Keep the straight-leg foot grounded and the bent knee aligned with the toes. Reduce the range if the groin or knee feels pinched.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in a staggered stance. Hold the handles, step one foot back and point both feet toward the anchor.

Keep the rear heel down and rear knee straight while bending the front knee and leaning the body forward. Hold the calf stretch, then return and switch legs; slightly bend the rear knee to bias the lower calf.
Keep the rear arch lifted and heel aimed straight back. Do not let the rear foot roll inward.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles lightly and step one foot into a long forward lunge.

Lower the hips, keep the rear leg long and rotate the chest toward the front leg as that-side arm reaches upward. Return the hand and chest to centre, push through the front foot to stand and repeat on the other side.
Keep the front heel grounded and knee aligned with the toes. Rotate through the upper back and hips rather than forcing the lower back.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet hip width. Hold the handles with arms long and soften the knees.

Hinge at the hips and fold the torso toward the thighs while allowing the arms to lengthen toward the anchor. Pause in a comfortable hamstring and back stretch, then bend the knees and roll or hinge back to standing.
Keep light strap tension and do not lock the knees. Stop if the stretch creates dizziness, numbness or sharp pain.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing away from the anchor in a staggered stance. Hold the handles and extend the arms overhead with the palms facing forward or inward.
Step forward and lengthen the hands upward and slightly back until a gentle stretch is felt through the shoulders, chest and sides of the torso. Breathe, then step back to release.
Keep the ribs down and glutes engaged. Reduce the reach if the lower back arches or the shoulders pinch.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral/hammer grip (palms facing each other), wrists straight and elbows lifted at shoulder height. Extend the arms while maintaining an active plank and strap tension.
Keep the palms facing each other and upper arms fixed as the elbows bend and the handles travel toward the temples. Extend slowly without dropping the elbows or losing the plank.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.

Set the straps to fully lengthened and kneel facing away from the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and arms extended in front of the shoulders. Align the knees, hips, shoulders and head in a braced plank.

Keeping the body straight from knees to head, bend the elbows and lower the chest between the handles. Press through the palms to return to straight arms without sitting the hips back or arching the lower back.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to fully shortened and position the body beneath the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing inward), wrists straight and hands beside the ribs. Depress the shoulders and use the feet for only as much assistance as needed.

Keep the shoulders down as the elbows bend and the body lowers between the handles. Press through the palms to straighten the arms; use the legs for assistance and stop before the shoulders roll forward.
Keep continuous strap tension and move at a pace that preserves balance and alignment. Start with a smaller range and stop the set when the position can no longer be maintained.

Set the straps to mid length in single-handle mode and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handle with a neutral grip (palm inward), wrist straight and elbow beside the ribs. Square the shoulders and hips and use the free arm for counterbalance.
Lower by bending the hips and knees while the knees track in line with the toes, then drive through the whole foot to stand. Use only enough arm assistance to preserve balance and position.

Keep the whole working foot grounded, track the knee in the same direction as the toes and use the handles for balance rather than pulling with the arms. Reduce depth or remove the jump until alignment is reliable.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet hip width. Hold the handles lightly, stand tall and keep equal pressure through the bases of the big and little toes.
Rise onto the balls of both feet by lifting the heels as high as possible without rolling the ankles. Pause, then lower the heels slowly to the floor and repeat.
Keep the knees straight but not locked and the body vertical. Use the straps only for balance; perform one leg at a time only after the two-leg version is controlled.
Set the straps to mid-calf and begin in a high plank facing away from the anchor with toes in the cradles, hands below shoulders and feet below the anchor.
Draw one knee toward the opposite elbow while rotating the pelvis slightly, then extend that leg fully as the other knee crosses toward the opposite elbow. Alternate in a smooth pedalling rhythm.
Keep the shoulders steady and press the floor away. Slow the cadence if the hips sag or the suspended feet begin to swing.
Set the straps to mid-calf and lie face-up with the heels in the foot cradles directly below the anchor. Press the heels down, brace the trunk and keep the pelvis level as the hips lift.
Maintain the hip lift and open the legs apart through a controlled range, then draw them together without allowing the pelvis to drop or rotate.
Keep the spine long and pelvis level; the effort should come from the hips and hamstrings rather than the lower back. Reduce the range if the straps slacken or the pelvis changes position.
Set the straps to mid-calf and lie face-up facing the anchor with heels in the cradles. Extend the legs, press the heels down and lift the hips into a straight reverse plank.
Bend one knee and draw that heel toward the glute while the opposite leg remains long. Extend the leg completely, then repeat with the other knee without lowering the hips.
Keep the pelvis level and shoulders relaxed. Reduce the range or lower the hips between repetitions if the hamstrings cramp.
Set the straps to mid-calf and begin in a high plank facing away from the anchor with toes in the cradles and hands below shoulders.
Bend both knees outward and draw them toward the outside of the elbows while keeping the soles of the feet facing each other as much as the straps allow. Extend both legs fully to return to plank.
Keep the shoulders over the hands and press the floor away. Use a smaller knee path if the hips drop or the groin feels pinched.

Set the straps to mid-calf and lie on the side, sideways to the anchor, with the feet secured in the foot cradles. Stack the supporting elbow under the shoulder, lengthen the body and set the hips and shoulders vertically.
Press the floor away and hold the body in one long line with the glutes and abdominals engaged. Keep the shoulders stable, pelvis level and straps still; lower to the ground with control.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor to place the toes in the foot cradles. Turn to the ground with the hands or forearms below the shoulders, feet directly below the anchor, and establish an active plank.

From the plank, bend one knee and rotate the pelvis so that foot reaches toward the opposite side behind the body. Return to a square plank before changing sides; move through the hips and upper back rather than twisting the lower back.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold both handles, straighten the arms and hinge the hips backward until the torso is nearly parallel to the floor.

With the spine long, reach the hands forward and slightly apart as the chest sinks between the arms. Hold the length through the shoulders, lats and upper back, then pull the hands toward the thighs and stand.
Keep the ribs controlled and shoulders away from the ears. Use a smaller hinge if the lower back rounds or the shoulders pinch.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with arms extended, then lower the hips behind the heels into the deepest comfortable squat while keeping the feet grounded. Adjust the feet slightly until the knees and hips feel comfortable.

From the bottom, bend the elbows into a biceps-curl position and keep the chest lifted. Press through the heels and midfeet to extend the knees and hips; use a controlled triceps press against the handles only as much as needed to assist the rise. Return to the bottom under control.
Keep the knees tracking with the toes and the heels down. The arms provide assistance, not the main force. Reduce depth if the spine rounds or the hips or knees pinch.

Fully lengthen the straps and stand facing away from the anchor. Place the straps under the arms, hold the handles beside the chest and lean forward about 45 degrees on the balls of the feet. Keep the body straight from head through heels.

Maintain the diagonal plank while bending the hips and knees to lower into a squat. Keep pressure through the straps and knees tracking with the toes, then drive through the balls and midfeet to extend the hips and knees to the starting angle.
Keep the hands connected to the chest and do not turn the exercise into a chest press. The torso and shins should remain nearly parallel.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Place the foot cradles around the backs of the hands with palms facing forward, wrists straight and elbows beside the ribs. Stand tall as if the head, spine, hips and heels are against a wall.

Keep the head, ribcage, hips and heels aligned as if against a wall. With the foot cradles around the backs of the hands and palms forward, slide the elbows and wrists overhead, then pull them back to the sides without arching or shrugging.
Use the straps only for support, keep breathing and stop before pain, numbness or joint pinching. Hold a steady position rather than bouncing.
TRX Alternating Forward Lunge with T/Y/I Fly
TRX Front Lunge with T/Y/I Fly
TRX Lunge with T Y I Fly

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with the arms extended and straps taut. Hold the handles with straight wrists; use palms down/inward for the Y and I paths and rotate to palms forward as the arms open into the T. Set the shoulders down before stepping.

Step forward into a controlled lunge while the straight arms perform the programmed fly: overhead and apart for Y, directly out to the sides for T, or beside the ears for I. Push through the front foot to return, lower the arms and alternate legs.

Keep the front foot grounded and knee tracking with the toes. Select one fly path at a time, keep the elbows straight and use a shallower lunge or more upright body angle until both parts remain controlled.

Set the straps to fully shortened and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and arms extended. Set the shoulders down and back and keep the body in an active plank before beginning the alternating high-low pull.

Lower the body with both arms straight. Pull one elbow high and the opposite elbow low so the hands separate vertically, then extend both arms and repeat with the positions reversed. Keep the body plank still as the arms alternate.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.
Fully shorten the straps and stand facing the anchor. Hold both handles palms down with arms extended and lean back in an active plank.

Row one handle toward the ribs while the opposite straight arm reaches to 12 o'clock overhead, 3 or 9 o'clock sideways, or 6 o'clock toward the hip as programmed. Return to two straight arms between reaches, then repeat on the other side.
Keep the pelvis and ribs square to the anchor. Use a more upright angle if the reaching arm causes the hips to rotate or the straps to slacken.

Set the straps to fully shortened and stand facing the anchor. Begin with the handles palms down and wrists straight for the high-row phase. Set the shoulders down and back and maintain an active plank; rotate the handles to a neutral grip for the low-row phase.

Pull the high row with palms down, elbows rising to shoulder height and hands finishing beside the shoulders. Extend the arms, rotate to a neutral grip and pull the low row with elbows close to the ribs and hands beside the lower chest. Return to straight arms before repeating or switching sides.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.

Set the straps to fully shortened in single-handle mode and stand facing the anchor with a wide stance. Hold the handle with a neutral grip (palm inward) and straight wrist, then extend the working arm across the body with controlled torso rotation.

Allow the working arm to extend across the body with controlled torso rotation. Drive the elbow back toward the ribs and rotate the chest toward the anchor, then reverse slowly while keeping the feet grounded.

Keep the straps taut, lead with the shoulder blades rather than the chin, and keep the hips from sagging. Begin more upright; walk the feet toward the anchor only when every repetition stays controlled.
TRX Squat Row to Y Fly

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with feet about hip-width. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing) for the row, wrists straight and arms extended. The hands rotate toward palms down/inward as the arms travel into the Y fly.

Lower into a squat with the arms extended. Stand and row the handles to the ribs with a neutral grip, then extend the arms and sweep them overhead into a Y as the palms rotate inward. Reverse the sequence under control.
Finish the row before beginning the Y fly; do not blend the phases by bending the elbows during the fly. Keep the knees aligned, ribs stacked and shoulders away from the ears.

Set the straps to mid length and lie face-up, centered beneath the anchor. Hold the handles beside the hips with palms pressing firmly down, wrists straight and arms long. Brace the trunk, lift the hips and begin with the legs extended together.

Press the handles down and raise the straight legs toward the anchor as the hips lift into the jackknife. Lower the hips with control, then roll the torso up into a balanced teaser with the legs elevated. Reverse each phase slowly without swinging.
Move slowly enough to keep the ribs and pelvis controlled. Shorten the lever by bending the knees or reduce the range if the lower back lifts or the movement becomes momentum-driven.
Set the straps to mid length and sit facing the anchor with both feet flat. Hold the handles palms up, extend the arms at shoulder height and lean back from the hips until the straps are taut.
Keep the upper arms parallel to the floor while bending the elbows and bringing the handles toward the temples. Slowly straighten the elbows without dropping the upper arms or rounding the back.
Sit tall on the sit bones, keep the wrists straight and shoulders down. Move the feet closer to the anchor for more resistance or farther away for less.

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and arms extended in front of the shoulders. Keep the elbows high and align the knees, hips, shoulders and head.
Keep the upper arms lifted and still while bending the elbows until the thumbs approach the temples. Press through the handles to straighten the arms, keeping the body aligned from knees to head.
Keep the straps off the arms, wrists straight and hips aligned with the shoulders. Use a more upright angle or shorter range if the lower back arches or the shoulders roll forward.

Set the straps to mid length and stand sideways to the anchor with both hands holding the handles together above the shoulder nearest the anchor. Use a wide stance and keep the arms long but not locked.

Rotate the hips and chest away from the anchor while sweeping the hands diagonally down across the body toward the opposite hip. Pivot both feet, then reverse the diagonal path under control to return the hands above the near shoulder.
Turn the hips, ribs and feet together. Keep the shoulders down and do not pull only with the arms. Perform low-to-high woodchops as a separately named variation.

Set the straps to fully shortened and position the body beneath the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing inward), wrists straight and arms extended. Use a stable low stance and keep the handles close to the ribs during the transition.
Pull the body upward, transition the chest over the handles as the elbows travel behind the body, then press to straight arms. Reverse the transition slowly and use the legs only as much as required.
Keep continuous strap tension and move at a pace that preserves balance and alignment. Start with a smaller range and stop the set when the position can no longer be maintained.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), wrists straight and arms extended. Maintain light tension and a tall posture before beginning the circles.
Guide the straight arms through smooth circles while the ribs stay stacked and the shoulders remain away from the ears. Use only a pain-free range and reverse direction with control.
Use the straps only for support, keep breathing and stop before pain, numbness or joint pinching. Hold a steady position rather than bouncing.
TRX Hamstring Curl with Weighted Crunch

Set the straps to mid-calf and lie face-up facing the anchor with the heels in the foot cradles. Hold a light weight plate or medicine ball against the chest, extend the legs and lift the hips until the body is straight from shoulders to heels.

Bend the knees and draw the heels toward the glutes while keeping the hips lifted. At the shortened position, exhale and curl the head and shoulder blades from the floor, bringing the ribs toward the pelvis. Lower the shoulders, then extend the legs slowly without dropping the hips.
Master the unweighted hamstring curl first. Keep the pelvis level, chin gently tucked and weight secured at the chest; stop if the hamstrings cramp or the neck takes over.

Set the straps to mid length and sit facing the anchor with the feet grounded. Hold the handles palms up/toward the face with straight wrists and elbows lifted at shoulder height. Lean back with the arms extended and straps taut.

Keep the elbows lifted as the hands curl toward the temples while the ribs draw toward the pelvis in a controlled crunch. Extend the elbows and torso together to return, keeping the feet grounded and straps taut.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Begin with a more upright body angle and use a smaller range until the arm path is consistent.
TRX Body Saw to Hip Abduction
TRX Body Saw with Hip Abduction
TRX Body Saw to Abductors Toes

Set the straps to mid-calf and kneel facing away from the anchor to place the toes in the foot cradles. Turn to the ground with the hands or forearms below the shoulders, feet directly below the anchor, and establish an active plank.

Glide the body backward from the shoulders and return to the starting plank, then open the suspended feet apart. Bring the feet together and fully reset the plank before repeating; keep the pelvis level through both phases.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.
TRX Hip Hinge to Y Fly

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles palms down with straight wrists and arms extended. Keep the straps taut, soften the knees and brace before hinging and raising the arms into the Y.

Push the hips back with the arms extended and spine long. Drive the hips forward as the straight arms sweep up and apart into a Y with thumbs leading slightly upward. Return the arms and hips together without shrugging.
Keep continuous strap tension and move at a pace that preserves balance and alignment. Start with a smaller range and stop the set when the position can no longer be maintained.
Set the straps to mid-calf and lie face-up facing the anchor. Place the heels in the foot cradles, bend the knees to about 90 degrees and lift the hips until the knees, hips and shoulders align.

Keep the hips elevated while slowly extending both knees and sending the heels away from the body. Stop before the pelvis drops or the lower back arches, then press the heels down and bend the knees to draw the cradles back beneath them.
Treat this as a long-lever posterior-chain exercise. Use a shorter leg extension or perform the standard hip press first if the hamstrings cramp or the pelvis cannot stay level.

Set the straps to mid-calf in single-handle mode and stand facing away from the anchor in a wide stance. Hold the handle palm down, extend the working arm in front of the shoulder and brace against rotation.

Keep the working elbow high and pointing forward while bending it until the thumb approaches the temple. Press through the handle and straighten the elbow completely without moving the upper arm or rotating the torso.
Keep the wrist straight, ribs controlled and strap clear of the arm. Use a more upright body angle before shortening the range.
TRX Biceps Curl to Clutch Curl
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor in an active plank. Begin with palms up, arms extended at shoulder height and elbows high.

Perform a standard biceps curl by bringing the hands toward the temples, then extend the arms. Lower the elbows beside the ribs, turn the palms inward and perform a clutch curl by drawing the handles toward the chest. Extend the arms and lift the elbows to reset.
Complete both phases without changing the body angle. Keep the shoulders down, wrists straight and straps taut throughout.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor. Hold the handles with palms forward and extend the arms overhead beside the ears. Stand tall with the straps taut.

Push the hips backward and hinge until the torso approaches parallel to the floor and the body forms an L shape. Keep the arms, back and legs long, then drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to return to standing with the arms overhead.
Keep the spine neutral and knees softly unlocked. Do not turn the hinge into a squat or arch the lower back at the finish.

Set the straps to mid-calf and lie on the side, sideways to the anchor, with the feet secured in the foot cradles. Stack the supporting elbow under the shoulder, lengthen the body and set the hips and shoulders vertically.

Lift into the side plank with the hips and shoulders stacked. Move the top foot forward and the bottom foot backward in a controlled scissor, then switch their positions without allowing the hips to drop or roll. Bring the feet together before lowering.
Press the floor away, keep the neck long and move only as far as the pelvis can stay controlled. To exit, lower the knees first, then remove the feet from the cradles.

Set the straps to mid-calf and lie face-up facing the anchor with the heels in the foot cradles and legs extended. Keep the hips resting on the floor, place the fingertips lightly behind the head or cross the arms over the chest and brace the abdominals.

Exhale and curl the head, shoulders and upper back from the floor, bringing the ribs toward the pelvis while the legs remain quiet. Pause, then lower the spine slowly until the shoulder blades return to the floor.
Keep the chin gently tucked and do not pull on the neck. The hips stay grounded; a bridged crunch is a separate variation.
Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with the straps taut. Hold the handles lightly, take a split stance and keep the torso tall and braced.
Drive through the front foot and switch the legs in the air, using the straps only for balance. Land softly in the opposite split stance with the knee aligned over the toes.

Keep the whole working foot grounded, track the knee in the same direction as the toes and use the handles for balance rather than pulling with the arms. Reduce depth or remove the jump until alignment is reliable.

Set the straps to mid length and lie face-up with the head toward the anchor. Hold the handles with palms facing the thighs, arms straight above the chest and wrists neutral; press down into the handles to create upper-body tension.
Press into the handles to create upper-body tension, then extend the opposite arm and leg away from the torso. Return and alternate sides while keeping the ribs down and lower back controlled.
Move slowly enough to keep the ribs and pelvis controlled. Shorten the lever by bending the knees or reduce the range if the lower back lifts or the movement becomes momentum-driven.

Set the straps to mid length and lie face-up, centered beneath the anchor. Hold the handles beside the hips with palms pressing firmly down, wrists straight and arms long. Lift the hips and brace the trunk before raising the legs.

Begin with the hips lifted and press the hands firmly into the handles. Keeping the legs straight, raise the toes toward the anchor, then lower with control while maintaining abdominal tension and shoulder stability.
Move slowly enough to keep the ribs and pelvis controlled. Shorten the lever by bending the knees or reduce the range if the lower back lifts or the movement becomes momentum-driven.

Set the straps to mid length and stand facing the anchor with the straps taut. Hold the handles with palms facing, center one foot with the anchor and extend the free leg forward; keep the chest lifted and use the straps only as much as balance requires.

Center the working foot with the anchor, extend the free leg forward and lower into a controlled pistol squat. Drive through the heel to jump, land softly on the same foot and regain alignment before repeating.

Keep the whole working foot grounded, track the knee in the same direction as the toes and use the handles for balance rather than pulling with the arms. Reduce depth or remove the jump until alignment is reliable.

Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Step one foot about half a stride forward and rest it on the heel with the toes pulled up and that knee straight. Bend the back knee about 15-20 degrees so most of the weight stays on the back leg, and rest both hands on the front thigh above the knee.

Keeping a neutral spine, hinge at the hips by pushing the hips straight back until a stretch is felt behind the front thigh, usually when the torso is 30-60 degrees forward. Hold 20-40 seconds with slow nasal breathing, letting the hips drift back a little further on each exhale, then press up through the back leg and switch sides.

Lead with the chest and push the hips back; rounding the low back moves the stretch away from the hamstring. Keep the front knee straight but not hyperextended. Rest the heel on a low step to increase the stretch.

Sit on the floor with one leg straight in front, kneecap and toes pointing to the ceiling. Bend the other knee and rest its sole against the inner thigh of the straight leg. Sit tall on the front of the sit bones with the hands on the floor beside the straight leg.

Inhale to lengthen the spine, then exhale and hinge forward from the hips over the straight leg, sliding the hands toward the shin, ankle or foot until a moderate stretch is felt behind the thigh. Hold 20-40 seconds, easing a little deeper on each exhale, then walk the hands back to sit upright and switch legs.

Keep the chest lifted and the belly moving toward the thigh; reaching farther by rounding is not the goal. Sit on a folded towel or block if the pelvis tucks under. Loop a strap around the ball of the foot if you cannot reach it, and keep the knee straight but soft rather than locked.

Lie on your back with both legs straight and the head resting on the floor. Loop a yoga strap, towel or band around the ball of one foot and hold one end in each hand with the elbows close to the floor. Press the back of the down leg into the floor with the toes pointing up.

Keeping the knee straight, raise the strapped leg toward the ceiling, then gently walk the hands down the strap to draw the leg toward you until a stretch is felt behind the thigh, typically at 70-90 degrees of hip flexion. Hold 30-60 seconds, then lower the leg slowly and switch.

Keep the opposite thigh pinned to the floor and the pelvis level; if it lifts, the stretch is coming from the low back instead. Relax the shoulders and neck. Bend the down knee with the foot flat to make it easier. Pull the toes toward the shin to add the calf and sciatic nerve.

Stand facing a flat bench or box between mid-shin and knee height. Place one heel on it with the leg straight and toes pointing up. The standing foot points straight ahead directly under the hip with the knee slightly soft, and both hip bones face the bench. Place the hands on the hips or on the raised thigh.
Keeping the back flat, hinge forward from the hips over the raised leg until a stretch is felt behind the thigh. Hold 20-40 seconds while breathing slowly, then come up tall and switch legs.

Choose a height that lets you keep a neutral spine; a lower surface is usually better than a high one. Keep the hip of the raised leg from hiking up toward the ribs by drawing it down and back. Rotate the toes slightly in to bias the outer hamstring (biceps femoris) or out to bias the inner hamstrings.

Stand tall next to a wall or rack and hold it with one hand for balance. Shift the weight onto the near leg with a soft knee. Bend the outside knee and grab the ankle or top of that foot behind you with the same-side hand.

Draw the heel toward the glute while keeping both knees side by side and the bent knee pointing at the floor. Then squeeze the glute of the stretching leg to tuck the pelvis slightly (posterior tilt) and bring the thigh just behind vertical until the stretch is felt along the front of the thigh and hip. Hold 20-40 seconds, release slowly and switch legs.

Do not arch the low back or let the bent knee drift forward or out to the side. Stand tall instead of leaning forward. Use a strap around the foot if you cannot reach it or if knee flexion is uncomfortable.

Lie on one side with the head resting on the bottom arm. Bend the bottom hip and knee to about 90 degrees in front of you to block the pelvis from rolling and the low back from arching. Bend the top knee and hold the top ankle or the top of the foot with the top hand.

Pull the top heel toward the glute, then squeeze the top glute and draw the thigh slightly backward so the knee moves behind the hip line until a stretch is felt along the front of the thigh and hip. Hold 30 seconds, release with control and roll to the other side.

Keep the top knee level with the hip rather than letting it drift up toward the ceiling. Keep the trunk long and the ribs down instead of arching. A good regression for people with poor standing balance; loop a strap around the foot if the hand cannot reach.

Kneel with your back to a wall or couch. Place one knee on a thick pad in the corner where floor meets wall, with the shin running vertically up the wall and the top of the foot against it. Step the other foot forward into a half-kneeling lunge so the front shin is vertical and that knee is over the ankle. Start with the hands on the front knee or on the floor.

Brace the abs, squeeze the glute of the back leg to tuck the pelvis, and slowly walk the torso upright toward the wall until a strong stretch is felt in the front of the back thigh and hip. Hold 1-2 minutes with slow breathing, then lean forward, carefully step out and switch sides.

Do not arch the low back to get upright; keep the ribs down over the pelvis. Regress by staying leaned forward with the hands on the front knee or moving the back knee farther from the wall. Pad the knee well.

Kneel on one knee on a pad with the other foot flat in front so both knees are at about 90 degrees, front knee over the ankle and the back knee directly under the hip. Keep the feet about hip-width apart for balance, stand the torso tall and place the hands on the hips.

Squeeze the glute of the down leg and tuck the pelvis under (posterior tilt) as if pulling the belt buckle up; for many people this alone creates the stretch. Keeping that tilt, shift the hips forward 2-5 cm until a stretch is felt at the front of the back hip. Hold 30-60 seconds, then switch sides.

The pelvic tilt creates the stretch; a big forward lunge with an arched back does not. Keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis and the torso vertical. Rotate the torso slightly toward the front leg to bias the psoas, or reach the down-leg arm overhead to add the side body.
Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch with Overhead Reach
Hip Flexor Stretch with Side Bend
Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch with Reach
Kneeling Hip Flexor and Lat Stretch

Set up in a half-kneeling position on a pad, both knees at 90 degrees and the back knee under the hip. Squeeze the back glute and tuck the pelvis. Raise the arm on the side of the down knee straight overhead with the palm facing in, the other hand on the front hip.

Shift the hips forward slightly into the hip flexor stretch, then reach the raised arm up and over toward the front-leg side, side-bending through the trunk so the stretch runs from the front of the back hip up through the side body and lat. Hold 20-30 seconds or move in and out for 6-8 slow reps, return upright and switch.

Lean sideways without rotating or arching the low back. Keep the glute switched on and the front knee tracking over the middle toes. Reach long through the fingertips as if lengthening the whole side rather than collapsing into the bend.

From hands and knees, bring one knee forward and place it on the floor just behind the same-side wrist, angling that shin diagonally across the body so the foot sits near the opposite hip. Slide the other leg straight back with the top of the foot on the floor and the kneecap facing down.

Square the hips toward the front of the mat and settle the weight evenly between both sides of the pelvis. Stay upright on the hands for a mild stretch, or walk the hands forward and lower the chest toward the forearms or floor until a deep stretch is felt in the front-leg glute and outer hip. Hold 30-90 seconds, press up and switch.
Keep the front foot flexed to protect the knee and stop if the front knee hurts. Place a block or cushion under the front-leg hip if it floats high,. Bring the front heel toward the groin to ease it.

Stand facing a bench, plyo box or table about hip height. Lift one leg and lay it on the surface with the knee bent and the shin across the front edge, the outer thigh and outer shin resting on top. The standing leg is straight with the foot pointing forward under the hip.

Square the hips to the bench, then hinge forward from the hips over the shin with a long spine, placing the hands on the bench, until the outer hip and glute of the elevated leg stretch. Hold 30-60 seconds, breathing slowly, then come up, step down and switch legs.

Easier on the knees and easier to control than floor pigeon. Keep the elevated foot flexed and the hips square. Bring the shin more parallel to the bench edge or step the standing foot back to intensify; let the knee rest on a towel if it hovers.

Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat, or straighten the bottom leg along the floor. Bring one knee toward the chest and hold it with the opposite hand on the outside of the knee and the same-side hand at the ankle.

Pull the knee diagonally across the body toward the opposite shoulder until a stretch is felt deep in the buttock and outer hip. Hold 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then return the foot to the floor and switch sides.

Keep the low back, pelvis and both shoulders on the floor; do not roll the hip up off the floor to get more range. Pull diagonally, not straight up toward the same shoulder. Stop short of any pinching in the front of the hip, and draw the knee less far across if it does.

Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat about hip-width apart. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to form a figure 4, with the crossed foot flexed and the crossed knee opening out to the side.

Lift the bottom foot off the floor, thread the same-side hand between the legs and the other hand around the outside, and clasp behind the bottom thigh or over the shin. Pull the bottom thigh toward the chest until the glute and outer hip of the crossed leg stretch. Hold 30-60 seconds, release and switch.

Keep the head and shoulders down; loop a strap around the thigh if the hands do not reach. Keep the tailbone heavy rather than curling up off the floor. Press the crossed knee gently away with the elbow to deepen, and keep the crossed foot flexed to protect the knee.

Sit tall near the front edge of a bench or chair with both feet flat and knees at about 90 degrees. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee so the outer ankle rests just above the knee, keep the crossed foot flexed and let the crossed knee open toward the floor.

Keeping the spine long, hinge forward from the hips, bringing the chest toward the crossed shin until a stretch is felt in the outer hip and glute. Hold 30 seconds with slow breathing, sit up and switch legs.

Lean with a flat back rather than slumping; the hinge creates the stretch. Press lightly down on the crossed knee for more stretch. A good desk-friendly option for clients with stiff hips or those who cannot get down to the floor.

Sit tall on the floor, bring the soles of the feet together and let the knees fall out to the sides. Draw the heels in to a comfortable distance from the groin, about a hand's length for most people. Hold the ankles or feet with both hands and sit on the front of the sit bones.

Lengthen the spine on an inhale, then exhale and hinge forward from the hips while letting the knees sink toward the floor until the inner thighs stretch. Hold 30-60 seconds, then sit up tall and release the legs.

Do not force the knees down hard with the hands or elbows; light pressure on the inner thighs is enough. Keep the spine long rather than rounding over the feet. Move the feet farther from the body for a gentler stretch, and sit on a cushion if the pelvis tucks under.

Start on hands and knees on a soft surface with pads under the knees. Slide the knees out wide, keeping the knees in line with the hips and the ankles directly behind the knees so each shin is parallel to the other, the knees bent 90 degrees and the inner edges of the feet on the floor.

Lower onto the forearms and slowly push the hips straight back toward the line of the knees until a strong stretch is felt in the inner thighs. Hold 30-90 seconds, or rock slowly forward and back for 8-12 reps, then shift forward and slide the knees in to exit.

Keep a neutral spine instead of letting the low back sag. Keep the hips level with the knees; if the hips drift behind the knees, the stretch shifts to the groin and can strain it. Rocking versions suit warm-ups; long holds develop range. Narrow the knees to reduce intensity.
Stand with the feet about twice shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly out. Place the hands on the hips or on the thigh of the leg that will bend.

Shift the weight to one side, bending that knee and sitting the hips back as in a side lunge while the other leg stays straight, until a stretch is felt along the inner thigh of the straight leg. Hold 20-30 seconds, push back to center and shift to the other side.
