Sit with the legs extended and together and the hands behind the hips, fingers pointing toward the feet. Press up into a reverse plank so the body is in a straight line from shoulders to heels, chest lifted.
Kick one straight leg up toward the ceiling with a pointed foot, then flex the foot and lower it with control. Alternate legs for 3-5 per side, then sit down.

Keep the hips level and high; squeeze the glutes and hamstrings of the supporting leg. Keep the chest open and avoid sinking into the shoulders. Bend the knees with the feet flat (tabletop) or just hold the reverse plank to scale.
Sit and balance just behind the sit bones with the knees bent and open, the soles together, and the hands threaded through the inside of the legs to hold the outsides of the ankles.
Clap the feet together three times, inhale and roll back to the shoulder blades and clap three times there, then exhale and roll forward to balance again. 6-8 reps.
Keep the C-curve shape constant; use the abs, not a kick, to roll back up. Do not roll onto the neck. A playful, lower-intensity rolling exercise often used to finish the mat sequence.

Sit with both knees bent and folded to one side (Z-sit), the feet pointing to that side. Hold the front shin or ankle with the hand on the side the feet point to, and rest the other hand on the floor.

Inhale and reach the arm opposite the feet up overhead, then exhale and side-bend toward the feet. Inhale back to center, then place that hand on the floor and reach the other arm overhead, side-bending away from the feet. 3-4 per side, then switch the leg fold.

Keep both sit bones as grounded as possible and lengthen up before bending. Breathe into the stretched side. Sit on a cushion if the hips are uneven, and add a gentle rotation toward the floor at the end of the side bend to open the back.
Lie on your back with the knees bent, the feet flat and parallel, hip-width apart and about a foot from the glutes, and the arms by the sides, palms down.

Exhale and tilt the pelvis back to flatten the low back, then peel the spine off the mat one vertebra at a time until the body is in a line from the knees to the shoulder blades. Inhale at the top, then exhale and roll down sequentially from the upper back to the tailbone. 6-10 reps.

Move slowly and articulate each segment rather than lifting as a block. Keep the knees pointing forward and hip-width. Do not overarch at the top. A gentler, mobility-focused version of the glute bridge.
Sit with the foot flat on the floor and the knee bent about 90 degrees, aligned over the second toe. Progress to standing on two feet, then one.

Without curling the toes, draw the ball of the foot toward the heel so the arch lifts and the foot shortens, keeping the big toe and heel on the floor. Hold 5-10 seconds, then relax. 10 reps per foot.
Keep the toes long and relaxed; curling the toes means the long toe flexors are taking over. Small, controlled movements only. Trains the intrinsic foot muscles that support the arch.
Sit on a chair with one foot resting on a hand towel laid flat on a smooth floor. The knee is bent about 90 degrees and the heel planted.
Curl the toes to grab and scrunch the towel toward you, then spread the toes wide and repeat until the whole towel is gathered under the foot. Flatten it out and repeat 2-3 times per foot.

Keep the heel down so the work stays in the toes and foot. Spread the toes wide between scrunches to train both directions. Place a light weight on the far end of the towel to progress. Useful in plantar fasciitis and ankle rehab programs.
Sit or stand tall with the spine neutral, the chin slightly tucked and the arms hanging loosely, or the elbows bent to 90 degrees at the sides.
Squeeze the shoulder blades back and slightly down toward the opposite back pockets, hold 5 seconds, then relax fully. 10-15 reps.

Do not shrug or push the ribs forward to fake the squeeze. Keep the chin tucked and the neck relaxed. A good posture break for desk workers. Progress to a band pulled apart in front of the chest while squeezing, or perform it lying face down.
Lie face down with the hands under the shoulders and the legs relaxed. Rest for a few breaths and let the back relax.

Press the upper body up by straightening the arms as far as comfortable while the hips and pelvis stay on the floor and the low back and glutes stay relaxed. Hold 1-2 seconds, exhaling to let the back sag further, then lower. 10 reps.

Let the low back sag; do not engage the glutes. Progress to full arm lockout only as tolerated. Stop and seek advice if leg symptoms spread further down the leg; pain moving out of the leg toward the middle of the lower back (centralization) is the response you want.
Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart. Place the palms on the back of the pelvis with the fingers pointing down, and squeeze the glutes lightly.
Lean back over the hands, extending the low back while the knees stay straight, as far as comfortable. Hold 1-2 seconds, then return upright. 10 reps.
Look forward or slightly up rather than throwing the head back. Keep the movement gentle and stop if pain travels into the leg. Useful as a break every 30-60 minutes during long sitting.
Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, hip-width apart and about 30 cm from the hips, the arms by the sides and the head relaxed.
Exhale and tilt the pelvis back so the low back flattens into the floor, drawing the pubic bone toward the ribs with the lower abs. Hold 5 seconds, then relax to neutral. 10-15 reps.
Use the abs, not a push from the legs; keep the glutes relaxed and the hips on the floor. Breathe out as you tilt. Progress to holding the tilt while marching one foot off the floor at a time.
Sit tall on a chair with the feet flat and the hands holding the edge of the seat.

Straighten one knee while tilting the head back to look up, then bend the knee while bringing the chin toward the chest. This slider pattern tensions the nerve at one end while slackening it at the other. Move smoothly for 10-15 reps per leg.
Move rhythmically, never into a strong stretch or a long hold. A mild pulling sensation is fine, but sharp, burning or lingering symptoms are not. Point and flex the ankle to adjust the tension.

Anchor a resistance band to a post at knee height. Step into the loop so it sits just behind one knee, then step back until the band is taut and pulls that knee forward into a slight bend, about 20-30 degrees. Keep the heel down.
Straighten the knee fully against the band by squeezing the quadriceps, hold 1-2 seconds at lockout, then slowly let the knee bend back to the start. 15-20 reps per side.

Keep the heel on the floor and the hips still. Squeeze hard at the top to work the end-range quad, especially the inner quad above the knee (vastus medialis). Keep the movement slow and the knee tracking over the middle toes.
Lean forward with one hand on a table and the other arm hanging straight down. Let the shoulder relax completely so the arm hangs like a rope.
Gently sway the body to let the hanging arm swing in small circles, then forward and back, then side to side. 30-60 seconds each direction.
Let the arm swing passively; the body sway drives it, not the shoulder muscles. Keep the circles small and pain-free. Common in early shoulder rehab to restore gentle motion.
Lie face down with a foam roller under the front of the thighs, supported on the forearms. Keep the body in a plank line from shoulders to knees with the core braced.
Pull and push with the arms to roll slowly, about 2-3 cm per second, from just above the knee to just below the hip. Pause 20-30 seconds on tender spots. Roll for 60-90 seconds per leg.

Roll one leg at a time for more pressure. Turn the leg in or out to target the outer and inner quads. Bend and straighten the knee while paused on a tight spot. Stay off the kneecap and keep the low back from sagging.
Sit with the roller under the back of the thighs and the hands on the floor behind you, arms straight and chest up so the weight shifts onto the legs.
Lift the hips and roll slowly from just above the knee to just below the sit bones, pausing on tight spots. 60-90 seconds per leg.

Cross one leg over the other to increase pressure. Turn the leg in and out to cover the inner and outer hamstrings. Bend and straighten the knee while paused on a tender spot. Avoid rolling directly on the back of the knee.
Sit with the roller under the calves and the hands on the floor behind you, arms straight and the core lightly engaged.
Lift the hips and roll from just above the ankle to just below the knee, rotating the leg to target the inner and outer calf. 60 seconds per leg.
Cross one leg over the other for more pressure. Keep the movement slow and pause on tender spots, pointing and flexing the ankle while paused. Avoid rolling hard directly over the Achilles tendon.
Lie on your side with the roller under the outer thigh, supported on the bottom forearm. Cross the top leg over in front with that foot flat on the floor to control pressure.
Roll slowly from just above the knee to just below the hip, pausing on tender spots. 60 seconds per side.

Use the top leg and arm to reduce pressure; this area is often very sensitive. The IT band itself does not lengthen or release, so roll slightly forward onto the outer quad and back onto the hamstring, and spend time on the small muscle at the front-outer hip (TFL).
Lie face down on the forearms with the roller parallel to the body on one side. Bring that leg out to the side with the knee bent about 90 degrees so the inner thigh rests on the roller.
Shift the body sideways toward and away from the roller to roll from just above the knee toward the groin, pausing on tender spots. 60 seconds per leg.
Keep the trunk still and roll slowly. Straighten the knee slightly to reach the longer inner-thigh muscles. Use moderate pressure and stop short of the pubic bone.
Sit on the roller and cross one ankle over the opposite knee, leaning onto the side of the crossed leg. Support yourself with the hands behind you and keep the other foot planted.
Roll slowly over the glute of the crossed leg, about 2-3 cm per second, pausing on tender spots. 60 seconds per side.
Lean into the target glute and rotate slightly toward the outer hip to reach the glute medius. Use a lacrosse ball for deeper pressure. Stay off the tailbone and low back.
Lie on your back with the roller across the upper back below the shoulder blades and the hands supporting the head, elbows in. Plant the feet hip-width apart and brace the core lightly.
Lift the hips and roll slowly from the mid-back to the tops of the shoulder blades, shifting slightly side to side to reach the muscles beside the spine. 60-90 seconds.
Keep the chin tucked and the head supported. Hug the arms across the chest to spread the shoulder blades for better contact. Do not roll the lumbar spine; use a ball for the low back muscles instead.
Lie on your back with the roller across the upper back at the bottom of the shoulder blades, the hands supporting the head with the elbows in and the feet flat with the glutes on the floor.

Keeping the hips down and the ribs tucked, extend the upper back over the roller, letting the head drop toward the floor, hold 2-3 seconds, then curl back up. Move the roller up one segment at a time. 5 reps per segment.

Keep the ribs down and the hips on the floor so the extension comes from the upper back rather than the low back. Exhale as you extend. Differs from rolling the thoracic spine by holding still and bending over the roller rather than rolling.
Lie on your side with the roller under the armpit area and the bottom arm extended overhead, thumb up. Bend the top knee and plant that foot in front to control pressure.
Roll from just below the armpit down to the bottom of the rib cage, rotating the chest slightly toward the floor and the ceiling to find tight bands. 60 seconds per side.
Keep the arm overhead and the pressure moderate. Roll slowly and stay out of the armpit itself to avoid the nerves and lymph nodes.
Lie face down with the roller under the front of one hip just below the hip bone, supported on the forearms. Move the other leg out to the side to shift the weight onto the target hip.
Roll slowly over the front and outer front of the hip, pausing on tender spots. 60 seconds per side.
Keep the core braced. Avoid rolling directly over the hip bone and do not roll into the abdomen. Bend and straighten the knee while paused. Use a softer roller if the area is sensitive.
Kneel on all fours with the roller under the shins, supported on the hands. Turn slightly to one side so the muscle on the outer front of the shin, not the bone, rests on the roller.
Roll from just above the ankle to just below the knee along the outer shin. 60 seconds per leg.

Keep the pressure light and avoid rolling on the shin bone. Roll one leg at a time for more pressure, and point and flex the ankle on tender spots. Useful after running or tibialis training. Stop if you feel sharp bone pain.
Sit on the floor with a lacrosse ball under one glute and the hands behind you. Cross that ankle over the opposite knee to put the glute and piriformis on stretch.
Roll slowly over the glute and deep hip rotators, pausing 20-30 seconds on tender spots. 60-90 seconds per side.

Use the hands and the planted foot to control pressure. Breathe into tender spots rather than tensing. If you feel tingling or shooting pain down the leg, move off the area, as the sciatic nerve runs nearby.
Sit, or stand holding a wall for balance, with a lacrosse ball under the arch of one foot. Start seated if the foot is sensitive.
Roll the foot slowly from the front of the heel to the ball of the foot, covering the inner, middle and outer arch, pausing on tender spots. 60 seconds per foot.
Control the pressure with body weight and add it gradually. Avoid rolling directly on the heel bone. A frozen water bottle is a cooler alternative. Pair with calf stretching.
Stand with the back against a wall, the feet about 30 cm from it, and place a lacrosse ball on the upper trap between the neck and the tip of the shoulder.
Lean into the ball and bend and straighten the knees slightly to roll it, pausing on tender spots. 60 seconds per side.
Stay on the muscle; avoid the neck, spine and collarbone. Use the wall angle to control pressure. Tilt the head away or move the arm across the body while paused to add a stretch.
Lie on your back, or stand against a wall, with a lacrosse ball under the back of the shoulder blade on the infraspinatus, below the bony ridge.
Roll slowly over the back of the shoulder blade and the rear deltoid, pausing on tender spots. While paused, move the arm across the body and rotate it in and out. 60-90 seconds per side.
Keep the pressure moderate and breathe. Stay off the spine and the bony ridge of the shoulder blade.
Stand facing a wall or door frame with a lacrosse ball under the chest, just below the collarbone and inside the front of the shoulder. Rest the arm against the wall.
Lean into the ball and roll it slowly, pausing on tender spots. Slide the arm up the wall or move it behind you to add a stretch. 60 seconds per side.
Avoid the collarbone, armpit and breast tissue. Use moderate pressure and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel tingling into the arm.
Sit at a table with a lacrosse ball on it and rest the forearm on the ball, palm down to start.

Roll the forearm from just above the wrist to just below the elbow, pausing on tender spots while opening and closing the hand. Then turn the palm up to work the flexor side. 60 seconds per side of each arm.
Use the other hand to add pressure. Move slowly. Roll both the extensors and the flexors, and avoid pressing on the inner elbow where the ulnar nerve runs.

Lie on your back with a peanut ball or two taped lacrosse balls under the base of the skull, one ball on each side of the spine. Bend the knees with the feet flat and let the head rest fully on the balls.
Relax the head into the balls and make tiny nods, like saying yes, then small turns side to side to work each side. Hold 60-90 seconds total.
Keep the pressure gentle and breathe. Stay on the base of the skull, not the neck vertebrae. Stop if you feel dizziness, numbness or an increasing headache.
Lie down or sit with the legs straight and the heels resting on the floor or a pillow.
Pull the toes up toward you as far as you can, then point them away as far as you can. Keep a steady rhythm, about 1 second each way.
Move the full range both ways. Often done 10 to 20 times every hour after surgery or bed rest to help circulation.
Sit with the leg straight. Loop a band around the inside edge of the forefoot and anchor it out to the side of the working foot (around the other foot or a fixed post).
Keeping the heel still, turn the sole of the foot inward against the band, then return slowly to the start.
Move only at the ankle; do not rotate the knee or hip. Slow and controlled, 2 to 3 sets of 10 to 15.
Sit with the leg straight. Loop a band around the outside edge of the forefoot and anchor it to the inside (around the other foot or a fixed post).
Keeping the heel still, turn the sole of the foot outward against the band, then return slowly to the start.
Works the muscles on the outside of the lower leg that protect against rolling the ankle. Move only at the ankle, slow and controlled.
Sit with the leg straight. Loop the middle of a band around the ball of the foot and hold the ends in your hands with light tension.
Point the foot away from you against the band as far as you can, pause, then let the foot return slowly toward you.
Keep the knee straight and the heel on the floor. A gentle way to strengthen the calf before standing calf raises.
Stand tall on the floor next to a wall or counter, feet hip-width apart, eyes forward.
Shift onto one foot and lift the other a few centimetres off the floor. Hold 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep the hips level and the standing knee soft. Spread the toes and grip the floor lightly. Progress by closing the eyes, turning the head or standing on a cushion.
Sit tall on the front half of a chair or bench, feet flat and hip-width apart, hands on the thighs or seat.
Lift one knee as high as you can without leaning back, pause, and lower the foot slowly. Alternate legs.
Keep the trunk upright and the core braced. Add an ankle weight or a band over the thighs to progress.
Stand next to a wall or counter. Place one foot directly in front of the other so the heel of the front foot touches the toes of the back foot.
Hold the position for up to 30 seconds without touching the support, then switch which foot is in front.
Stand tall with the eyes forward. Easier: feet half overlapped (semi-tandem). Harder: close the eyes. Stay near support for safety.
Sit or stand barefoot with the feet flat and hip-width apart.
Lift the big toe while pressing the four smaller toes into the floor, then switch: press the big toe down and lift the four smaller toes. Alternate slowly.
Keep the ankle and the rest of the foot still. It is normal for this to be hard at first; use a hand to help until it comes.
Lie on your back, head and shoulders curled up, legs straight to the ceiling.
Lower one leg toward the floor as the other comes toward you, pulse twice, then switch.
Keep the lower back down and the curl steady.
Lie on your back with the head and shoulders curled up, legs in tabletop.
Circle the legs as if pedaling backward, extending one long as the other bends.
Move slowly. Keep the pelvis still.
Stand tall at the back of the mat.
Roll down to the floor, walk the hands out to a plank, do one to three push-ups, walk back and roll up.
Keep the elbows close in the push-up. Roll through the spine.
Sit leaning back on the hands with the legs lifted together in a V.
Circle the legs to one side, down and around, then reverse.
Advanced. Keep the chest lifted and the circles controlled.
Sit on one hip with the legs bent or straight and stacked, hand under the shoulder.
Press up into a side plank with the top arm reaching overhead, then lower with control.
Lift from the bottom waist. Keep the shoulder stable.
Sit with straight legs crossed at the ankles, hands by the hips.
Roll back into a roll-over, switch the leg cross, roll up to a teaser, reach the arms behind, then fold forward.
From a roll-over, hold one foot with both hands and lift the other leg toward the ceiling.
Scissor the legs, switching which foot you hold.
Advanced. Weight on the shoulders, not the neck.
Lie face down, bend the knees and hold the ankles.
Lift into a bow and rock forward and back on the front of the body.
Advanced. Lift through the chest and press the feet into the hands.
Side plank on a straight arm with the legs straight and stacked.
Lift the top leg and arm into a star, then swing the leg forward and back.
Advanced. Keep the hips lifted and stable.
Start on hands and knees, knees hovering an inch off the mat.
Hold the hover and extend one leg back at a time.
Keep the hips level and the back flat.
Stand with the feet hip width or together, weight even through both feet, arms by the sides.
Lengthen up through the crown, lift the kneecaps lightly and breathe steadily for 5 to 10 breaths.
Stack the ribs over the pelvis. Soft knees, relaxed shoulders.
Lie on your back with the legs relaxed apart and the arms by the sides, palms up.
Close the eyes and let the body fully relax for 3 to 10 minutes.
Support the knees or head if needed. Let the breath be natural.
Lie on your back, soles of the feet together and knees falling open.
Rest here for 1 to 3 minutes, breathing into the hips.
Support the knees with blocks if the stretch is strong.
From Warrior I, clasp the hands behind the back.
Bow the torso inside the front knee, letting the arms lift overhead, then rise.
Keep the front knee over the ankle. Hips stay level.
From downward dog, bring one knee behind the wrist and lay the shin across the mat, back leg long.
Settle the hips, then fold forward over the front leg for 1 to 2 minutes each side.
Keep the hips square. Pad under the front hip if it lifts.
Squat on the toes, twist and place both hands on the floor outside one thigh.
Lean forward until the feet lift, balancing on bent arms, then lower.
Look forward, not down. Use a block under the head if learning.
Kneel and interlace the fingers, forearms on the mat, crown of the head down cupped by the hands.
Walk the feet in, lift one leg then the other to stack the hips over the shoulders, hold, then lower with control.
Weight mostly on the forearms. Learn near a wall with a teacher; avoid with neck issues.
Start in dolphin pose with the forearms parallel.
Kick or float the legs up to balance on the forearms, hold, then lower one leg at a time.
Press the forearms down and lift out of the shoulders. Learn at a wall.
From downward dog, lift one leg and flip the body to open into a backbend, top foot landing behind.
Reach the top arm overhead and lift the hips, then flip back.
Keep the bottom shoulder stacked over the wrist.
Lie on your back with a strap around one foot, that leg straight up.
Hold the stretch, then let the leg open out to the side, and return.
Keep the other leg heavy and the hips level.
From a standing forward fold, shift onto one leg.
Lift the other leg toward the ceiling as the chest folds toward the standing leg, hold, then lower.
Keep the hips squared to the floor. Blocks under the hands help.
Lie on the carriage, head on the headrest, shoulders against the blocks. Heels on the footbar hip width, legs parallel, knees bent.
Press the carriage out until the legs are straight without locking, then return slowly against the springs.
Keep the pelvis neutral and the ribs down. Push evenly through both heels. Choose springs that let you control both directions; lighter is not always easier.
Lie on the carriage with the balls of the feet on the footbar, heels lifted, legs parallel and knees bent.
Press out to straight legs keeping the heels high, then bend the knees to return with control.
Keep the heels lifted at one height the whole way. Knees track over the second toe.
Lie on the carriage, heels together on the footbar and toes apart in a small V, knees bent and turned out from the hips.
Press the carriage out, squeezing the heels and inner thighs together, then return slowly.
Turn out from the hips, not the knees. Keep the heels glued together.
Press the carriage out to straight legs with the balls of the feet on the footbar.
Lower the heels under the bar, then rise as high as possible onto the toes. Keep the legs straight.
Move only at the ankles. Keep the carriage still.
Press out to straight legs with the balls of the feet on the footbar.
Bend one knee as that heel drops under the bar while the other heel lifts, then switch in a smooth running rhythm.
Keep the carriage still and the pelvis level. Breathe steadily.
Lie on the carriage holding the straps, arms up toward the ceiling, legs in tabletop or extended at 45 degrees.
Curl the head and shoulders up as the arms press down beside the hips, then pump the arms while breathing in for five counts and out for five, ten times.
Keep the lower back on the carriage. Lower the legs only as far as you can keep the back down.
Lie on the carriage with the straps around the arches, heels together, knees bent and open in a diamond.
Press the legs out on a diagonal until straight, squeezing the inner thighs, then bend back to the diamond with control.
Keep the pelvis still and the tailbone down. Heels stay together.
Lie on the carriage with both feet in the straps, legs straight toward the ceiling.
Circle both legs down, out, around and together, keeping them straight. Reverse after five.
Make the circles only as big as you can keep the pelvis still.
Lie on the carriage with feet in the straps, legs straight up. Arms long by the sides.
Lift the hips and roll the legs over until parallel to the floor, bend the knees, then roll down the spine one bone at a time and extend the legs out to return.
Advanced: avoid with neck or back problems. Control the roll with the abs, not momentum.
Lie on the carriage with the balls of the feet or heels on the footbar, knees bent.
Peel the spine up into a bridge, then press the carriage out and in from the bridge, and roll down to finish.
Keep the hips level and the ribs soft. Drive through the heels for hamstrings.
Place the long box on the carriage and lie face down, chest just past the front edge, holding the straps with straight arms reaching forward.
Pull the straps back past the hips as the chest lifts slightly, then return with control.
Lead with the shoulder blades. Lift the chest only as far as the lower back allows.
Lie face down on the long box holding the straps with arms out to the sides in a T.
Sweep the arms back toward the hips in a wide arc as the chest lifts, then return slowly.
Keep the arms straight and the neck long. Light springs.
Lie on the long box on your back holding the straps, head and shoulders curled up, knees to chest.
Reach arms and legs to the ceiling, open them wide, circle the arms down to the hips, then return to the start.
Keep the curl and the lower back down throughout. Advanced coordination move.
Sit on the long box or carriage holding the straps, legs lifted in a V.
Roll back partway with control and return to the V balance, keeping the legs still.
Advanced. Keep the chest lifted and the shoulders down.
Sit tall on the carriage facing the footbar, legs straight or crossed, holding the straps.
Pull the elbows back to row, then round forward and reach to return with control.
Sit tall on the sit bones. Keep the shoulders away from the ears.
Sit facing the straps (back to the footbar) holding them at the chest, spine tall.
Round back into a C-curve, open the arms out to the sides, sit tall and circle the arms forward to return.
Scoop the belly in the C-curve. Keep the arms moving with the breath.
Sit tall facing the straps, holding them with palms up and elbows straight in front.
Curl the hands to the shoulders keeping the elbows still, then straighten slowly.
Sit tall without leaning back. Light spring.
Kneel on the carriage facing the straps, holding them with straight arms in front.
Press the arms back past the hips, turn the head side to side, return the head to center and let the arms return slowly.
Stay tall through the hips; do not sit back. Light springs.
Kneel on the carriage facing the straps, arms straight in front at shoulder height, palms up.
Curl the hands toward the forehead keeping the elbows still, then extend slowly.
Hold the torso still and upright.
Kneel on the carriage with the hands on the footbar, back rounded, feet against the shoulder blocks.
Push the carriage back with the legs and draw it in with the abs, keeping the back rounded and the upper body still.
Move only the legs. Pull in with the belly on the return.
Kneel on the carriage with the hands on the footbar, back flat, feet against the shoulder blocks.
Push the carriage back and draw it in while keeping a flat back.
Keep the ribs knitted. Smaller range if the lower back arches.
From the knee stretch position, lift the knees an inch off the carriage.
Press the carriage back and in small pulses, knees hovering.
Advanced. Keep the hips level and the back rounded.
Stand on the carriage, heels against the shoulder blocks, hands on the footbar, hips high in an upside-down V.
Push the carriage back with the legs and draw it in using the abs, keeping the upper body still.
Keep the heels down if you can. Rounded back variation deepens the core work.
Plank with hands on the footbar and the balls of the feet against the shoulder blocks.
Push the carriage back a few inches from the shoulders and return, keeping a straight line from head to heels.
Do not let the hips sag. Small range first.
Kneel on the carriage with the hands on the footbar, chest lifted in a gentle backbend.
Press the carriage back with the legs while keeping the arch, then pull it back in with the abs.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears. Lift through the sternum, not the lower back.
Start in a pike with the hands on the footbar and feet against the shoulder blocks.
Shift forward into a plank, then pull the carriage in back to the pike using the abs.
Advanced. Keep the arms straight and the shoulders over the wrists in the plank.
Sit side-on on the carriage with legs folded, one hand on the footbar.
Press the carriage out as you side bend over the footbar, reach the other arm overhead, then return.
Lengthen before you bend. Keep both sit bones heavy.
Stand with one foot on the carriage against the shoulder block and the other on the standing platform, facing sideways, arms out.
Slide the carriage out by pressing the legs apart, then draw it in with the inner thighs.
Keep the hips square and the torso upright. Light spring, small range first.
Stand with the front foot on the platform and the back foot against the shoulder block, hands on the footbar or hips.
Push the carriage back with the back leg into a lunge, then draw it in with control.
Keep the front knee over the ankle. Stay tall.
Stand on the floor beside the frame, one foot on the platform and the other on the carriage against the shoulder block, hands on the footbar, knee bent.
Push the carriage back with the moving leg in small or full kicks while the standing leg stays bent.
Keep the hips level and the standing knee steady.
Lie on your side on the carriage, head on the arm, bottom leg bent and top foot on the footbar.
Press the carriage out with the top leg until straight, then return slowly.
Keep the hips stacked. Do not roll back.
Lie on the carriage with one foot on the footbar and the other leg in tabletop.
Press the carriage out with one leg and return slowly. Finish all reps, then switch.
Keep the pelvis level and both hips heavy.
Sit at the front of the carriage facing the footbar, feet on the bar, hands holding the front edge, back rounded.
Press the carriage out by straightening the legs, then lift the heels, bend the knees and draw it back in.
Hold the C-curve without moving the torso.
Sit at the front of the carriage, hands on the frame beside the hips, balls of the feet on the footbar.
Lift the hips and press the carriage out, then draw it in while lifting the hips into a pike.
Advanced. Keep the arms straight and the shoulders down.
Lie face down on the long box, hands on the footbar.
Press the carriage away and lift the chest into extension, then return slowly.
Lengthen the spine before lifting. Keep the glutes lightly engaged.
Lie on the carriage, feet on the footbar, then lift the legs toward the ceiling.
Roll the legs overhead, bend the knees and roll down the spine, then return the legs to the bar.
Advanced: avoid with neck or back issues.
Plank with hands on the standing platform and feet on the carriage against the shoulder blocks.
Lift the hips and draw the carriage in to a pike, then lower back to plank.
Keep the arms straight and the shoulders over the wrists.
Fit the jump board instead of the footbar and lie on the carriage, feet on the board in parallel.
Jump the carriage away and land softly on the board, rolling through the feet.
Land quietly through toe-ball-heel. Keep the head and spine still.
Lie on the carriage, feet on the footbar, hips lifted with the lower back against the bar side of the carriage.
Lower the spine through a bridge while the carriage moves, then roll back up and reverse.
Advanced. Move slowly through each segment of the spine.
Sit tall on the chair with the balls of the feet on the pedal, knees bent, hands by the hips.
Press the pedal down and let it rise slowly, keeping the upper body still.
Sit tall on the sit bones. Control the pedal on the way up.
Sit side-on on the floor beside the chair, one hand on the pedal.
Press the pedal down as you side bend over the chair, reach the other arm overhead, then lift back.
Keep both sit bones down. Lengthen before bending.
Stand behind the chair with the hands on the pedal, pressing it down.
Lift the hips into a pike to raise the pedal, then lower with control.
Advanced. Keep the arms straight and the shoulders over the wrists.
Stand facing the chair, one foot on the pedal, hands on the hips.
Press the pedal down with the working foot and let it rise slowly, standing tall.
Keep the hips level and the standing knee soft.
Stand facing the chair, one foot on the seat and the other on the pedal.
Step up onto the seat as the pedal rises, then lower with control without letting the pedal drop.
Keep the hips square. Press through the top foot.
Lie face down over the seat with the hands on the pedal.
Press the pedal and lift into extension, then lower slowly.
Lengthen first; lift through the chest.
Sit on the front edge of the chair, facing away, hands on the pedal behind you.
Bend the elbows to lower the pedal, then straighten to lift it.
Keep the elbows pointing back and the chest open.
Sit on the floor facing the chair, legs straddling it, hands on the pedal.
Round forward vertebra by vertebra to press the pedal down, then restack to sitting.
Scoop the belly; do not just bend at the hips.
Sit on the seat with the hands on the pedal behind or in front, legs lifted in a V.
Roll back partway as the pedal rises, then return to the balance.
Stand beside the chair, the near foot on the pedal.
Press the pedal down as you bend the standing leg into a side lunge, then rise.
Keep the torso upright and the standing knee over the toes.
Stand in chest-deep water, tall posture.
Walk forward heel to toe, swinging the arms, then walk backward.
Keep the core engaged and the posture upright. Longer strides add resistance.
Stand in waist- to chest-deep water.
Jog in place driving the knees high, arms pumping.
Land softly on the balls of the feet. Keep the chest tall.
Stand in chest-deep water, arms by the sides.
Jump the feet apart while sweeping the arms out, then back together.
Push and pull the water with the arms for more work.
Stand in chest-deep water, feet shoulder width.
Squat down and jump up, landing softly back into a squat.
Low-impact plyometric: the water cushions the landing.
Stand in waist- to chest-deep water.
Step forward into a lunge, then push through the front foot to the next step.
Keep the torso upright and the front knee over the ankle.
Stand side-on in chest-deep water, knees soft.
Shuffle sideways across the pool and back.
Stay low and keep the toes forward.
Stand in chest-deep water facing the wall, hands on the edge shoulder width.
Bend the elbows to bring the chest to the wall, then press back.
Keep the body in a straight line.
Hold the pool edge with both hands, body floating face down or on your back.
Kick the legs in quick, straight-legged flutters from the hips.
Kick from the hips, not the knees. Keep the ankles loose.
Stand side-on to the wall, one hand on the edge.
Swing the outside leg forward and back, then out to the side and across.
Stand tall; let the water slow the swing.
Stand in chest-deep water holding foam dumbbells, arms down, palms forward.
Curl the dumbbells up toward the surface, then push them back down.
The water resists both ways: biceps up, triceps down. Elbows stay at the sides.
Stand in shoulder-deep water, arms out to the sides just under the surface holding foam dumbbells.
Sweep the arms together in front, then open them back out.
Keep a slight elbow bend. Faster sweeps add resistance.
Stand in shoulder-deep water holding foam dumbbells by the sides.
Raise the arms out to the sides to just under the surface, then press them back down.
Buoyancy lifts for you; the work is pushing down. Keep the shoulders relaxed.
Stand in chest-deep water holding foam dumbbells at the surface in front of the chest.
Press the dumbbells down to the thighs, then let them float up with control.
Brace the core so the dumbbells do not lift you.
Sit on a pool noodle like a swing in deep water, upright.
Pedal the legs as if riding a bike, moving across the pool.
Stay upright; arms can scull for balance.
Float on your back with a noodle under the arms or knees.
Draw the knees toward the chest, then extend the legs long.
Move slowly; the water rewards control.
In deep water wearing a flotation belt, body upright.
Run with a full running motion without touching the bottom.
Lean slightly forward. Drive the knees and push back with the feet.
Jump and pull both knees toward the chest, then land softly.
Low impact; focus on height and soft landings.
Scissor the legs forward and back while swinging the opposite arm, alternating in rhythm.
Long, straight-leg strides. Push the water with open hands.
Stand with your back against the pool wall in chest-deep water.
Slide into a squat with the thighs near parallel and hold.
Keep the knees over the ankles. Breathe steadily.
In chest-deep water, press a kickboard down under the surface with straight arms, feet back in a long line.
Hold the board steady under the water.
Brace the core so the board does not tip.
In deep water, sit upright as if on a chair.
Circle the legs alternately to stay up, hands sculling at the surface.
Keep the torso upright and the circles continuous.
Hold the pool edge with both hands, body angled down, feet on the wall.
Drive the knees alternately toward the chest at a quick pace.
Keep the shoulders over the hands.
Stand in waist- to chest-deep water holding the edge.
Rise onto the toes, pause, then lower slowly.
Good for early rehab; progress to one leg.
Stand facing the wall, holding the edge.
Curl one heel toward the glute, then straighten the knee. Switch legs.
Keep the thighs in line; move only at the knee.
